localChanges: Each terrain's page in the Civilopedia now says what a square of it gives, what irrigation, a mine, a road or a railroad adds, what it costs to move onto it, how much it helps a defender, how long each job takes your Settlers and what irrigating, mining or transforming turns it into, in Civilization I and II games (closes #620).

log: The movement, strength and terrain job rules describe each terrain's movement cost, its defence bonus, how many turns a Settlers takes to irrigate, mine, build a road or a railroad on it, and what clearing or planting a forest turns it into, with core-rule's Description. The conversions' action rules, made by base-unit-action-rules, are wrapped to say so. The road and railroad job factors are exported constants. Requires core-rule 0.1.11.

The tile yield rules describe each terrain's food, shields and trade, what Irrigation, a Mine and a Road add to it, and a Railroad's +50% on any land square, with core-rule's Description. Ocean's and River's trade, the Road's trade and the Railroad's share are exported constants the rules read. Requires core-rule 0.1.11.

Each terrain's movement cost, defence multiplier, work turns per job (with whose work they are) and the terrain that irrigating or mining it makes now carry Descriptions read from the same civ2-world tables the rules use. The move, air-and-naval and described terrain job MovementCost rules are built here, as base-unit-movement builds them and in their place, with the Description among their own items, so a move pays nothing for it. The irrigate and mine conversion table moves to lib/terrainConversions so the action rows and the job turns share it.

Each terrain's tile yield, irrigation and mine bonuses, road trade, railroad shield bonus and transform result now carry Descriptions read from the same @TERRAIN rows and constants the rules use. The road's trade and the railroad's bonus are lifted to exported constants; the transform conversions are wrapped with lib/describedRule.
